newsitem.title: DENMARK: Copenhagen bourse and futures market to merge.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen bourse and futures market to merge.

text.p: The Copenhagen Stock Exchange and the city's Futop futures and options markets are to merge, in an effort to cut costs and attract more foreign investors, a joint statement said on Thursday.

It said that, subject to approval by bourse shareholders at an October 29 meeting, Futop would become a public company, to be a wholly-owned subsidiary of the stock exchange. Among synergies would be a 10 percent cut in staff during 1997.
Futop, whose turnover fall 50 percent in 1995, said last January that it might need a partner to survive and London's LIFFE and the Stockholm OM markets were rumoured prospects.

Bourse Chairman Hans Ejvind Hansen told Reuters that the takeover fulfilled his wish to keep derivative trading in Copenhagen and in creating a unified marketplace for all instruments he hoped it would boost overall turnover.
"We hope -- especially with regard to the overseas client -- that being able to go to one place, instead of several as before, will stimulate the Danish securities market," he said.

"The merger will not have any immediate implications for customers, neither positive nor negative but we certainly hope it will give the Danish securities market a boost," he added. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
